correctness.rationale: An exact induction establishes all subset sums of 2,...,m. Each integer in the middle range has a connected explicit witness via star spokes plus one tail chord. The middle intervals concatenate because T_m>=n+4; singleton and deleted-vertex witnesses cover both ends. The parameter m<=n-4 makes all chords legal, and algebra gives the claimed sqrt(2n)+O(1) bound. The standard-library checker independently exercised all claimed finite checks and returned VERIFY_OK; finite tests are not used in the infinite proof.

residual_risks: An unindexed contemporaneous manuscript or subsequent stronger version may contain a comparable bound; targeted searches are not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: This answers a specific open sublinearity question in the contemporaneous motivating paper, replacing its linear general bound by a uniform, explicit O(sqrt n) construction. The core interval-tiling idea supplies connected witnesses for every target and links a natural consecutive-integer subset-sum lemma with sparse graph completion. This is structural progress, not a relabeling or isolated computation.
